Forms of EMD and PBG Bidders can also submit the EMD with Fixed Deposit Receipt made out or pledged in the name of A/C Senior Divisional Finance Manager, Bengaluru Division, South Western Railway . The bank should certify on it that the deposit can be withdrawn only on the demand or with the sanction of the pledgee. For release of EMD, the FDR will be released in the favour of the bidder by the Buyer after making endorsement on the back of the FDR duly signed and stamped along with covering letter. Bidder has to upload scanned copy/ proof of the FDR along with bid and has to ensure delivery of hardcopy to the

Buyer within 5 days of Bid End date/ Bid Opening date 4. Forms of EMD and PBG Successful Bidder can submit the Performance Security in the form of Account Payee Demand Draft also (besides PBG which is allowed as per GeM GTC). DD should be made in favour of Senior Divisional Finance Manager, Bengaluru Division, South Western Railway payable at Bengaluru . After award of contract, Successful Bidder can upload scanned copy of the DD in place of PBG and has to ensure delivery of hard copy to the original DD to the Buyer within 15 days of award of contract. 5. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses ADDITIONAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS (ATC) Outcome-based colony sanitation activities (colony cleaning and solid waste management) at BNC Colony, outcome-based housekeeping acti vities at Railway Health Unit, Bangalore Cantonment and general clean ing services at BNC Colony for a period of two years. (To be read as Buyer-Added Special/Additional Terms and Conditions on the GeM Bid) 1. General 1.1 Scope of work, eligibility criteria on financial turnover, similar nature of work experience, Performan ce Guarantee (PG) and other conditions placed in the Tender Document (uploaded as Scope of Work / Job Description), together with the Buyer-added Special Terms and Conditions, shall be binding on thi s contract. The tenderer must read in detail all conditions placed in the uploaded tender document a nd in these Buyer-added Special and Additional Terms and Conditions. The default conditions placed i n the Bid Document for Scope of Work, eligibility criteria on financial turnover, similar nature of work experience, ePBG and other conditions shall not be binding on this contract. 1.2 The tenderer has to read and abide by all the General, Special and other conditions specified in the tender document made available here, including the General Conditions of Contract (S), 2018 and Ge M Terms and Conditions, including conditions on all taxes applicable to this contract. 1.3 The tenderer should have its registered office in the State of Karnataka, preferably in Bengaluru, as geographic proximity to the Divisional Railway Hospital, Bengaluru will be beneficial to both the tend erer and the Buyer. 2. Eligibility Criteria 2.1 Work Experience: The bidder should have satisfactorily completed, in the last three previous financi al years and the current financial year up to the date of opening of the tender, one similar single serv ice contract for a minimum of 35% of the advertised value of the bid. Note: A “completed service contract” includes an on-going service contract, subject to payment of bills amounting to at least 35% of the advertised value of the bid. 2.2 “Similar service contract” means Maintenance/execution of housekeeping works & waste managem ent/ Mechanized cleaning & conservancy services including waste management / Colony sanitation w orks including segregation & disposal of all types of waste from Railway colonies / any work of above- mentioned type and this work should have been executed in not less than 500 residential units in an y residential colony of Railway Central Govt./ State Govt./ PSU establishments. The work should have been executed as per Central Pollution Control Board/ State Pollution Control Board norms. 2.3 The bidder/firm must submit proof of satisfactory performance along with certified copies of the abo

ve-mentioned works. Tenderers should submit appropriate certificates clearly mentioning all the par ameters required to fulfil the minimum eligibility criteria for executed/executing work of a similar nat ure. 2.4 The tenderer has to qualify on account of minimum eligibility (execution/executing of similar nature of work and holding sufficient financial turnover) to be considered further for evaluation. Tenderers who do not possess the required minimum eligibility criteria on execution/executing of similar nature of work will be considered technically unresponsive and no further evaluation will be carried out. 2.5 All documents required to substantiate the claim for minimum eligibility criteria should be enclosed /submitted in the bid document. All documents are subject to verification. 3. Financial Standing The bidder will be qualified only if it has the minimum financial capability set out below: 3.1 T1 – Annual Turnover: The bidder should have an annual financial turnover not less than 1.5 times t he advertised bid value during the last three previous financial years and in the current financial year up to the date of opening of the tender. The audited balance sheet reflecting financial turnover, certif ied by a Chartered Accountant with stamp, signature and membership number, shall be considered. 3.2 T2 – Liquidity: The bidder should have access to, or have available, liquid assets, lines of credit and other financial means to meet cash flow, valued at 5% of the estimated bid value net of the applicant 's commitments for other contracts. The audited balance sheet and/or banking reference, certified b y a Chartered Accountant with stamp, signature and membership number, shall be submitted by the bidder along with the bid. The banking reference should clearly state the amount the bank is in a position to lend for this work t o the applicant/member of the Joint Venture/Consortium. Where the Net Current Assets (as seen from the balance sheet) are negative, only the banking reference will be considered; otherwise, the aggreg ate of the Net Current Assets and the submitted banking reference will be considered for working out the liquidity. Note: For calculation of liquidity, only the audited balance sheet of the current financial year 2026 –27 (as the tender is proposed to be opened in October 2026) and/or the previous financial year 2 025–26 will be considered; the T2 liquidity document should be uploaded accordingly. The banking reference should be from a Scheduled Bank in India and should not be more than 3 mont hs old as on the date of submission of bids. 4. Undertaking 4.1 The bidder shall submit, along with the tender documents, an undertaking as per Annexure 8 of the Tender Document, certifying the truthfulness of all documents submitted/uploaded along with the te nder. This is mandatory for all bidders. Failure to submit the undertaking shall result in summary reje ction of the bidder's offer. 5. Performance Guarantee (PG) 5.1 Performance Guarantee at the applicable rate of the contractual value (see Clause 6 below for the r evised rate) shall be deposited by the successful bidder, in four separate equal parts, within 30 (thirt y) days from the date of issue of the Letter of Acceptance (LOA). Extension of time for submission of PG beyond 30 days, and up to the date of actual submission, may be granted by the Authority compe tent to sign the contract agreement; however, a penal interest of 15% per annum shall be charged fo r the delay beyond 30 days, i.e., from the 31st day after the date of issue of the LOA. If the contracto r fails to submit the requisite PG within 60 days from the date of issue of the LOA, a notice shall be se rved to deposit the PG immediately, not exceeding 90 days from the date of issue of the LOA. If the c ontractor fails to submit the requisite PG even after 90 days from the date of issue of the LOA, the co ntract shall be terminated, duly forfeiting the EMD and other dues, if any, payable against that contra ct; the failed contractor shall be debarred from participating in the re-tender for that work. If the 60t h day is a bank holiday or office closure, the next working day shall be considered the last day for su bmission of the PG. The decision of the Authority competent to sign the Contract Agreement shall be final in case of any dispute. (Clause No. 4.11.1 of GCC for Service.) 5.2 The value of PG to be submitted by the contractor will not change for a price variation of up to 25% (either increase or decrease). If, during execution, the value of the contract increases by more than 2 5% of the original contract value, an additional Performance Guarantee amounting to 10% of the exc ess value over the original contract value shall be deposited, in four equal parts, by the contractor. C onversely, if the value of the contract decreases by more than 25% of the original contract value, Per

formance Guarantee amounting to 10% of the decrease in contract value shall be returned to the co ntractor. Any PG amount held by Railways in excess of the PG required for the decreased contract va lue shall be returned to the contractor, duly safeguarding the interest of Railways. (Clause No. 4.11.2 of GCC for Service.) 5.3 The applicable Performance Guarantee shall be calculated as per the revised value of the contract, covering all variations, up to the determination of the contract. (Clause No. 4.11.3 of GCC for Service. ) 5.4 If the penalty imposed exceeds 50% of the applicable maximum penalty (as per the revised value of the contract), a PG equivalent to 25% of the applicable PG shall be forfeited. If the penalty imposed e xceeds 75% of the applicable maximum penalty, a PG equivalent to 50% of the applicable PG shall be forfeited. The PG shall be encashed after completion of the contract. (Clause No. 4.11.4 of GCC for Se rvice.) 5.5 The successful bidder shall submit the Performance Guarantee (Clause No. 4.11.5 of GCC for Servic e), amounting to the applicable percentage of the contract value, in any of the following forms: (1) A deposit of cash; (2) Irrevocable Bank Guarantee; (3) Government Securities, including State Loan Bonds, at 5% below market value; (4) Deposit Receipts, Pay Orders, Demand Drafts and Guarantee Bonds — of either the State Bank of India or any Nationalised Bank; (5) Guarantee Bonds executed, or Deposit Receipts tendered, by any Scheduled Bank; (6) A deposit in the Post Office Savings Bank; (7) A deposit in National Savings Certificates; (8) Twelve-year National Defence Certificates; (9) Ten-year Defence Deposits; (10) National Defence Bonds; and (11) Unit Trust Certificates at 5% below market value or at face value, whichever is less. A Fixed Deposit Receipt (FDR) in favour of Sr. DFM/SBC/SWR (free from any encumbrance) may also b e accepted. The instruments listed above will also be acceptable for guarantees in the case of Mobiliz ation Advance. 5.6 The Performance Guarantee shall be submitted by the successful bidder after the LOA has been iss ued, but before signing of the contract agreement. The PG shall initially be valid up to the stipulated date of completion and the maintenance period (if any), plus 60 days beyond that. If the time for com pletion of service is extended, the contractor shall get the validity of the PG extended to cover such e xtended time for completion and the maintenance period (if any), plus 60 days. (Clause No. 4.11.6 of GCC for Service.) 5.7 The Performance Guarantee shall be released after physical completion of the work/service delivery , based on a Completion Certificate issued by the competent authority stating that the contractor has completed the assigned services satisfactorily in all respects, and on passing of the final bill based o n a No Claims Certificate from the contractor. Where a contract provides for a warranty/maintenance clause, 25% of the Performance Guarantee shall be retained until the warranty/maintenance period is over and a certificate to that effect is issued by the Manager. (Clause No. 4.11.7 of GCC for Service.) 5.8 Whenever the contract is rescinded, the Performance Guarantee shall be encashed/forfeited. The ba lance work or services shall be got done independently, without risk and cost to the failed contractor. The failed contractor shall be debarred for a period of 2 years from the date of such rescindment fro m participating in the bid for delivery of the balance services of the failed contract. If the failed contr actor is a partnership firm, every member/partner of that firm shall similarly be debarred for 2 years, in their individual capacity. (Clause No. 4.11.8 of GCC for Service.) 5.9 The Manager shall not make a claim under the Performance Guarantee except for amounts to which the President of India is entitled under the contract (notwithstanding, and without prejudice to, any o ther provisions in the contract agreement), in the event of: (a) Failure by the contractor to extend the validity of the Performance Guarantee as described ab ove, in which event the Manager may claim the full amount of the Performance Guarantee. (b) Failure by the contractor to pay the President of India any amount due — whether agreed by th e contractor or determined under any clause/condition of the Agreement — within 30 days of se rvice of notice to this effect by the Manager. (c) The contract being determined or rescinded under the provisions of the GCC, in which case the Performance Guarantee shall be forfeited in full and shall be absolutely at the disposal of the Pr esident of India.

(Clause No. 4.11.9 of GCC for Service.) 6. Revision in Rate of Performance Guarantee 6 . 1 Railways, in accordance with the directives issued by the Ministry of Finance on the subject of Performance Guarantee to be submitted by tenderers, and as per the Railway Board directive vide Le tter No. 2017/EnHM/25/11 dated 24.05.2024 issued by Director/EnHM/RB, have revised the rate of Pe rformance Guarantee as below. Existing Percentage of PG Revised Percentage of PG 10% 5% 6.2 As per the illustrated Clause 4.11 of GCC(S), the standard PG is 10%; this has been revised to 5%, a nd continues at 5% for service contracts. As the present tender — “outsourcing the outcome-based c olony sanitation activities (colony cleaning and solid waste management) at BNC Colony, outcome-b ased housekeeping activities at Railway Health Unit, Bangalore Cantonment and general cleaning ser vices at BNC Colony for a period of two years” — is a service tender, and as the applicable PG rate (1 0%, 5%, or any other value decided by the Railway Board) may change in future, the tenderer must keep itself appraised of the applicable rate and submit the PG governing the contract within the stipul ated period as mentioned in Clause 5 above. 7. MSME/Udyam Registration Certificate — EMD/Tender Cost Exemption 7.1 Tenderers claiming EMD/tender cost exemption by submitting an MSME/Udyam Registration certific ate should submit/upload the relevant MSME certificate for services pertaining to the services tender ed, under the appropriate/corresponding field only. If placed under any other field, it will be consider ed by GeM as non-submission of EMD, and the tender will be evaluated accordingly as per extant Ge M rules. Offers of tenderers seeking EMD/tender cost or any other exemption/preference by submitti ng non-relevant MSME/Udyam Registration certificates will be summarily rejected, as this will be con sidered non-submission of EMD/tender cost. Tenderers are accordingly requested to understand in d etail the services for which the tender is called, peruse the tender document in detail, and submit MS ME/Udyam Registration certificates relevant/similar to this tender for any exemption/preference soug ht. 8. Jurisdiction and Dispute Resolution 8.1 All disputes are subject to the jurisdiction of the High Court of Karnataka, or its subordinate courts a t Bengaluru, only. Before approaching the court, the existing internal mechanism of arbitration shoul d be explored as a mandatory first step. .
